title: Sweat a copper water joint: heat it until the solder melts at a touch, feed it full, stop before the flux burns
instruction: A vertical 1/2 in copper water-tube joint stands in a pipe vise: the top tube is pushed into a cleaned and fluxed coupling. A lit hose torch lies on its rest and a small coil of 1/8 in lead-free solder wire stands in its holder, its straight end down. Sweat the joint: heat it with the torch, its flame on the base of the coupling's cup, never into the cup's mouth or onto the solder's end. Touch the end of the solder to the joint where the top tube enters the coupling; it melts only once the joint is hot enough. Once it melts, feed solder into the joint until a ring of solder shows all round the joint's edge (about 8 mm of the wire). Do not overheat the joint, which burns the flux. Then take the solder and the torch away from the joint (the flame's tip at least 8 cm from the base of the cup), keeping each held up or back on its stand, and let the joint cool undisturbed until the solder sets.
context: Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (510,600 US workers, O*NET 47-2152); a core task: "Assemble pipe sections, tubing, or fittings, using couplings, clamps, screws, bolts, cement, plastic solvent, caulking, or soldering, brazing, or welding equipment". CDA, Soldering and Brazing Copper Tube and Fittings: "touch the solder to the joint. If the solder does not melt, remove it and continue heating." "Do not overheat the joint or direct the flame into the face of the fitting cup." "small drops may appear behind the point of solder application, indicating the joint is full" "Experience will indicate the amount of heat and the time needed." Unlike a TIG weld, where the arc shows the heat and filler is dabbed per segment, the joint's heat is hidden and found by touch, inside a window: solder flows only past its liquidus, the flux burns past 600 F (our rule, the top of its rated range), and the solder sets round a wire left on as it cools.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Fixed (one bench; the coupling's lower joint is already soldered): a pipe vise (60 mm square, 30 mm tall) at x 0.25, y 0 holding a vertical 1/2 in Type L copper tube (0.625 in OD) in a wrought coupling whose top (the cup's mouth) is 65 mm over the table; a top tube (0.625 in OD) sits 0.5 in deep in the cup and stands 30 mm over it (0.004 in clearance, cleaned and fluxed). The torch's rest (a block under its handle) and the solder's holder (a block with a 10 mm square well, 56.5 mm deep) at (0.3, -0.12). Loose: a lit hose torch (0.28 kg, a 22 mm square handle 110 mm long, a burner tube and nozzle; its flame's inner cone 165 mm ahead of the handle's grip point, which lies at (0.075, 0.215) with the flame heading -49.5 deg from +x); a coil of 1/8 in 95-5 solder wire (45 g, 24 mm across, 18 mm tall) with a 55 mm straight end standing down in the holder's well. The joint's temperature starts at 70 F. With the flame's inner cone on the cup's base (the flame's mark, facing the torch) the joint heats toward 1050, 850 or 720 F by seed (time constant 25 s), reaching the solder's liquidus after about 13, 18 or 23 s of steady heat; the heat falls off with the inner cone's distance d from the mark as exp(-d^2 / (2 (25 mm)^2)), and the joint cools by Newton's law. Nothing in the scene shows the seed. The wire's end rests on the joint's face, a spring (0.8 N/mm) under the coupling's top; while the wire's end is on the joint's edge (its inner edge within 1.2 mm of the top tube) and pushes the face 0.5 mm or more below the solder's level and the joint is at or over 464 F, solder melts in at up to 5 mm of wire per second and the face sinks with it (up to 12.5 mm). Full: 8.1 mm of wire fed (CDA Table 1: 0.32 in of 1/8 in wire for a 1/2 in joint at 0.004 in clearance); then a ring of solder shows round the joint's edge. If the flux burns, a dark ring shows there.
scoring: Melting: solder melts into the joint only while the wire's end is on the joint's edge (its inner edge within 1.2 mm of the top tube and the lowest point of its end within 0.5 mm of the face) and pushes it 0.5 mm or more under the solder's level, and the joint is at or over 464 F (the solder's liquidus); fed = the length of wire melted in. Full: 8.1 mm or more fed. Set: the joint under 452 F (the solidus). Away: the flame's inner cone 8 cm or more from the mark (the cup's base on the torch side) and the wire's tip 3 cm or more from the centre of the coupling's mouth, each tool back on its stand (its frame within 20 mm of its start) or held up (its frame 80 mm or more over the table), not let go on the bench. Success (1.0, held 1 s): full, set, away. Partial credit at the last step, each needing the one before: full, set and away but not yet held 1 s 0.8; full 0.6; half full (4.1 mm) 0.5; any solder melted in 0.25; else 0. Scored 0 from then on: the flux burnt (the joint over 600 F at any time), the solder set round the wire (the wire's tip still on the face after solder went in, as the joint cooled through 452 F), the flame on the joint's edge or the solder's end (our rule for the CDA caution: the inner cone within 10 mm of the coupling's mouth ring or the wire's tip, even when sweeping), the torch or the wire 30 mm below the table top, or the heat model not running (an error, or not stepping with the run).
reset_notes: The torch on its rest and the wire in its holder; the joint at room temperature with no solder in it, the face at its top and both rings hidden; the heat rate by seed. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. PhysX has no heat or melting: the joint's temperature, the flame's heat and the solder are our model. The flame is drawn only; the wire does not shorten, its tip sinks as a spring face at the joint's edge is lowered (the top cup is drawn only). The flame is held on one mark and solder fed at one point (CDA sweeps the flame and makes overlapping passes); no capillary flow or fillet. Heat rates, falloff and cooling are estimates, set so the seeds' melt and burn times do not overlap.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 33.9 s, step 678)
